t65z20_fg1p1w7p1: For lots of people, healing gets around to some forgiveness eventually, or at least to not living under the resentment anymore. You can't put it on a schedule. And you don't need it first to be safe (please don't wait for it), or to set boundaries. Making them answer for it can come first, and so can justice, and so can getting better. Resentment does shrink what you can see, though. It keeps your little one circling the injury. But if you push yourself to forgive before you're there, you get a nice show of being at peace, and the hurt just goes underground.

t65z20_fg1p3w8p1: That doesn't make what they did okay, and in theory there were other things they could have done. But punishing them now can't reach back and give them what they were missing then, the sense to see it or the help they needed. Or the skills. What's left is fixing what can be fixed, and making it easier for something different to happen now. They still have to answer for it, and it still hurt. Keeping your limits can still be right. So can the law, if it comes to that, and saying plainly that it was wrong, and keeping away from them, for good if you need to. You can understand them and still hold them to it. You can forgive them and never talk to them again. "I understand how you became this way" can sit right next to "I now understand why I shouldn't rely on you for this."

t65z20_st1p6w7p1: Love moves in a loop. It goes from spiritual experience to your little one, on into the grown-up relationship, from you into other people, and back again. Maybe you're not sure which door you came in through. The loop matters more than the door. Community can work in both directions. Sometimes the people come first. They love you, you feel safe with them and like you belong, and something deeper has room to open. Other times the opening comes first and changes who turns up in your life (some people call that "manifesting"). Then community is how it gets practical and real, down into your body.
